newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Feb. 10, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Sequent Computer Systems Inc will announce general availability of NUMA-Q, a highly scalable server, one that will become more affordable as Sun Microsystems Inc and others churn out commodity designs to lower costs, PC Week reported Feb. 10.
Netscape Communications Corp this year will revamp its Directory Server software with advanced LDAP support and new tools for writing directory-enabled applications, PC Week reported Feb. 10.

COMPUTERWORLD - Microsoft Corp is shifting its application development focus from the desktop to the server and last week unveiled Visual Basic Version 5.0 with an eye toward creating applications that sit on the server, Computerworld reported Feb 10.

The latest plan by the IRS to cope with its well-publicized technology woes would replace some aging systems in the short term and outsource tax return data entry in the long term, Computerworld reported Feb. 10.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - International Business Machines Corp and Eastman Kodak Co are building a Web-based system for managing, storing and distributing high-quality digital images, CRN reported Feb. 10.

Microsoft Corp and Netscape Communications Corp are in the throes of unveiling new strategies for gaining share in the "extranet" market of business to business communications over the Internet, CRN reported Feb. 10.

INFOWORLD - Novell Inc plans a major release of its GroupWise product code-named Jolt that will include Internet protocol support and Web publishing features, InfoWorld reported Feb. 10, citing unidentified sources.

Intel Corp has told vendors that the next-generation Pentium Pro chip code-named Klamath will not be delivered until May or early June, pushing back expected system deliveries by at least a month to July or later, InfoWorld reported Feb. 10.

INFORMATION WEEK - Bull HN Information Systems plans to bring out a new version of its systems security product, ISM/OpenMaster, primarily targeted at U.S. banking and insurance companies, Information Week reported Feb. 10.
Baan Co NV plans a major release of its enterprise resource planning software by the end of 1997, Information Week reported.

EE TIMES - Avant! Corp this week will introduce technologies, products and programs that hammer home its intent to become a front-ranking broadline electronic data automation provider, EE Times reported Feb. 10.

The new version of Virtual Reality Modeling Language (VRML 2.0) promises to relieve the bandwidth constraints that have held back the market growth of 3-D interactive worlds on the Internet, EE Times reported Feb. 10.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Intel Corp will have trouble meeting demand for some flash memory parts in the first half of 1997, but buyers can take heart from knowing that there are plenty of other suppliers eager to take up the slack, analysts told Electronic Buyers News on Feb. 10.

Plans by South Korean DRAM chip makers to cut 16-megabit production could backfire, because most of their competitors are either increasing output or maintaining current product levels, EBN reported Feb. 10.
